extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners (participants in ex parte reexamination)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules and evaluation criteria governing ex parte reexamination proceedings before the USPTO, including interviews, disclosure duties, notification of concurrent proceedings, merger of multiple reexaminations, and interactions with interferences/Board proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure under 37 CFR 1.555
rubrics_metrics.description: Any fraud practiced or attempted on the Office or any violation of the duty of disclosure through bad faith or intentional misconduct by any such individual results in noncompliance with 37 CFR 1.555(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All such individuals who fail to comply do so at the risk of diminishing the quality and reliability of the reexamination certificate issuing from the proceeding. See MPEP § 2282 and § 2686 for related duties to disclose prior or concurrent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews location and scheduling (37 CFR 1.560)
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews in ex parte reexamination proceedings must be conducted in the Office at such times, within Office hours, as the respective examiners may designate; interviews will not be permitted at any other time or place without the Director's authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be arranged in advance. In-person interviews must be at Alexandria or an Office satellite location (when building security permits public admission), unless the Office of Patent Legal Administration authorizes otherwise. Telephone interviews initiated by the examiner are possible but with limitations (see other entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of interviews regarding patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews for the discussion of the patentability of claims in ex parte reexamination proceedings will not be conducted prior to the first official action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: interviews prior to the first Office action are permitted only where the examiner initiates the interview for the purpose of providing an amendment which will make the claims patentable and the patent owner's role is passive (limited to agreeing to the change and not otherwise discussing merits).

rubrics_metrics.name: No third-party participation in ex parte interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests that reexamination requesters (third parties) participate in interviews with examiners will not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party requesters cannot attend or participate in ex parte interviews. Support staff (paralegal or legal instruments examiner) may telephone a requester to discuss filing-date compliance issues, but substantive merits discussion with non-owners is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner written statement after interview (37 CFR 1.560(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance of an interview with an examiner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written statement must be filed as a separate part of a response to an outstanding Office action, or as a separate paper within one month from the date of the interview, whichever is later. The requirement cannot be waived; failure to file the written statement as required will result in termination of the reexamination prosecution (per 37 CFR 1.550(d)). A patent owner's response to an outstanding Office action after the interview does not remove the necessity for filing the written statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on communications with non-owner parties (what is 'procedural')
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any party who is not the patent owner requests information as to the merits of a reexamination proceeding, the examiner will not conduct an interview to provide that information; only questions on strictly procedural matters may be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for 'procedural matter': (A) information obtainable by reading the file (open to the public) is procedural and may be discussed; (B) matters not available from reading the file are considered to relate to merits and may not be discussed. Parties should be referred to CRU SPRS or TC QAS for strictly procedural questions. Example: when the next Office action will be rendered is a merits-related question and should not be answered to a non-owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex Parte Interview Summary form PTOL-474 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must complete an Ex Parte Interview Summary form PTOL-474 for each interview held where a matter of substance has been discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A copy should be given to the patent owner at the conclusion of the interview; the original should be made of record in the reexamination file, and a copy should be mailed to any third-party requester. Preliminary copies submitted for consideration will be attached to the PTOL-474 and made of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-interview submissions to facilitate special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner desires to initiate an interview, the patent owner should initially contact the examiner to indicate issues to be discussed and determine if an interview will be granted; if granted, the patent owner must file at least three (3) working days prior to the interview an informal written statement of the issues and an informal copy of any proposed claims to be discussed, unless the examiner waives the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit copies by facsimile or hand-carried to avoid delay. The informal copies considered by the examiner will be made of record as an attachment to PTOL-474. These steps provide structure to the interview and facilitate the statutory mandate for special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview duration and extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: The duration of the interview will not exceed one hour, unless the patent owner files a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 showing sufficient cause where more time is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner may, at their sole discretion, extend the duration to discuss issues the examiner deems appropriate. In reexamination, an hour in a structured interview should ordinarily be sufficient; extensions require good cause or examiner discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of interviews after an Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one interview may be requested after an Office action and prior to filing the response to that action, absent a showing of good cause to conduct a second interview during this period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The good-cause showing must explain why the information could not have been presented sooner given the special dispatch requirement. After a final rejection, a party requesting a second interview must provide an advance showing that it will 'convince' a reasonable examiner that it will expedite the issues for appeal or disposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565)
rubrics_metrics.description: In an ex parte reexamination proceeding, the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings in which the patent is or was involved such as interferences, reissues, ex parte reexaminations, inter partes reexaminations, or litigation and the results of such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure a complete file, the Office will accept copies of notices of suits and other proceedings and copies of decisions or papers filed in courts involving the patent. However, submissions must be limited to bare notice of the prior or concurrent proceedings; they must not include arguments or other materials beyond notice. Highlighting or marking goes beyond bare notice. Copending reexamination/application copies should not be submitted; instead provide identifying numbers and status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office handling of notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proper submission pursuant to 37 CFR 1.565(a) will be promptly entered into the record of the reexamination file, and will be considered by the examiner as to its content, when the proceeding comes up for action on the merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office deems the volume of submitted papers too extensive or not enterable, it may return, expunge, or discard all or part of the submission. Persons submitting must limit their submission to notification only, or submissions will be returned/expunged/discarded at the Office's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraphs to remind duty under 1.565(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 22.07 or 22.08, if appropriate, may be used to remind the patent owner of the continuing duty under 37 CFR 1.565(a) to apprise the Office of any litigation activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶22.07 is for patent owner requests or Director-ordered reexamination; ¶22.08 is for third-party requester situations. Examiner notes indicate when these paragraphs should be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for granting a second/subsequent ex parte reexamination request
rubrics_metrics.description: In order for a second or subsequent request for ex parte reexamination to be granted, a substantial new question of patentability must be raised by the art (patents and/or printed publications) cited in the second or subsequent request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2240 for discussion on determining whether a substantial new question of patentability is raised. The second request is decided based on the claims in effect at the time of the determination (37 CFR 1.515(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: CRU Director decision and process for merger of copending reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: If the second or subsequent request is granted, the decision on whether to combine the proceedings will be made by the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) Director (may be delegated to CRU SPRS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines: process Request 2 quickly and assign it to the same examiner as Request 1; hold requests until patent owner's statement and requester reply or until filing time expires; CRU Director prepares merge decision. No decision to combine should be made until reexamination is actually ordered in the later-filed request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when reexaminations are merged
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings are merged, the patent owner is required to maintain identical claims in both files and identical amendments in the merged reexamination files for the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responses and other papers filed in the merged proceeding must consist of a single response addressed to both files, filed in duplicate, each bearing a signature and containing identifying data for both files. Both files remain separate complete files though prosecution is handled at the most advanced point possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to make claims identical after merger
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment to make the claims the same in each file is required by the merger decision but is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all of the merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph, as being indefinite as to the content of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection is for failure to particularly point out the invention. Patent owner will be given 1 month to provide the housekeeping amendment to make claims identical when required by the merger decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution stage processing for merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: When prosecution in merged proceedings occurs, a single combined examiner’s action will be prepared; each action will contain the control number of the two proceedings on every page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single action cover form (with both control numbers) will be used; clerical staff will print appropriate data on originals and copies. Each requester receives a copy of the action; the patent owner gets copies. When a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate is appropriate, it will be printed for the merged proceeding and scanned into the merged files. File processing follows MPEP § 2287.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of proceedings (merger-related and general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension of a proceeding will only be granted in extraordinary instances because reexamination proceedings must proceed with 'special dispatch' (35 U.S.C. 305); express written approval of the CRU or Technology Center Director must be obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension will not be granted when there is an outstanding Office action. Example uses: allow time for owner’s statement and requester’s reply prior to merging, or await a court decision when appropriate—but only rarely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper is filed which requires payment of a fee (e.g., excess claim fee, petition fee, appeal fee, brief fee), only a single fee need be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although only one fee is paid, copies must be filed for each file in the merged proceeding where required (e.g., copies of briefs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to merge multiple copending reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge multiple reexamination proceedings is necessary since the Office will generally sua sponte make a decision to merge; petitions filed prior to the determination and order to reexamine on the second request will not be considered but will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the patent owner can file a petition to merge any time after the order to reexamine on the second request, better practice is to include such petition with the patent owner’s statement under 37 CFR 1.530. A third-party requester of a reexamination proceeding does not have standing under statute to file a petition to merge; the requester may file a notification of concurrent proceedings instead. All decisions on merits of petitions to merge are made by the CRU Director (or delegate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on copending reexamination and interference proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: General policy: a reexamination proceeding will not be delayed or stayed because of an interference or the possibility of an interference, due to the requirement of 35 U.S.C. 305 that reexamination proceed with special dispatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may suspend the reexamination or the interference under certain conditions (e.g., motion to suspend interference presented to and denied by administrative patent judge and request for suspension filed within ten days of denial). The Board (37 CFR 41.103) can tailor solutions for copending reexamination and interference; decisions in the interference will consider the status of the reexamination proceeding. Note statutory point: a reexamination proceeding itself can never be 'involved' in an interference because a reexamination is neither an application nor a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 41.8 mandatory notices relating to Board proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: In an appeal brief or at the initiation of a contested case, and within 20 days of any change during the proceeding, a party must identify: (1) its real party-in-interest, and (2) each judicial or administrative proceeding that could affect, or be affected by, the Board proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For contested cases, a party seeking judicial review must file a notice with the Board of the judicial review within 20 days of filing the complaint or notice of appeal and include a copy of the complaint or notice of appeal. See also 37 CFR §§ 1.301–1.304.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of examination before initiating contested case (37 CFR 41.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before a contested case is initiated, except as the Board may otherwise authorize, for each involved application and patent: (a) Examination or reexamination must be completed, and (b) There must be at least one claim that (1) is patentable but for a judgment in the contested case, and (2) would be involved in the contested case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement ensures that contested cases (e.g., interferences or appeals) proceed only where examination/reexamination is at a stage permitting meaningful Board consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board jurisdiction over involved files (37 CFR 41.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board acquires jurisdiction over any involved file when the Board initiates a contested case; other proceedings for the involved file within the Office are suspended except as the Board may order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This suspension allows the Board to control resolution of contested issues and coordinate with reexamination status as needed.
